correctness.rationale: Cubicity identifies the forbidden faces with the full incident three-stars. In the repair, the cover of the edge Alexander dual has nerve the vertex-independence Alexander dual, via natural mutually reversing face-poset maps with composites containing their inputs. Both integral Alexander dualities introduce an ambient permutation sign. The rotation and reflection have traces +1 and -1 on independence H_1, and signs (-1,-1) on the graph vertices and (+1,-1) on the graph edges, respectively. The resulting H_5 signs are -1 and -1 and determine the action on the integral rank-one group. The graph group is the full sixteen-element dihedral group by four-cycle incidence, also checked exhaustively. Subdivision and exact rational coinvariants give the quotient criterion, including subgroups contained in the kernel. Nonequivariant simple connectivity follows by filling the loops of missing triangles with cones, so the duality homology calculation also recovers the background sphere.

replay.evidence: Of all 4096 edge subsets the face vector is (12,66,212,423,516,352,108,7), with 52 dimension-six and seven dimension-seven facets. The 847 nonempty Morse pairs leave critical masks 1 and 2646, and the Hasse sort visits all 1696 nonempty faces. Testing all 8! permutations gives exactly 16 graph automorphisms. Exhaustive signed sums on admissible invariant edge-cycle unions yield alternating chain traces (0,0,0,1,0,0,0,1) for r and (2,4,-8,-7,12,6,-6,-1) for s. The augmentation gives reduced Lefschetz number +1 for each, hence H_5 sign -1 for both; the full sixteen-element character was checked. The packaged replay also ran successfully. The frozen script was inspected, not executed.

residual_risks: The calculation is specific to the Wagner graph and its graph-automorphism action. It establishes no equivariant sphere model or integral quotient homology. The ordinary quotient conclusion is an algebraic deduction over Q, not part of the enumeration.

evidence: The edge-star dual's nerve is Ind(W)^*. Applying the two combinatorial Alexander dualities shifts the reduced homology of Ind(W) by four degrees; filling missing-triangle boundaries in M_2(W) yields simple connectivity and therefore the sphere from the known S^1 result.

The nonequivariant S^1 theorem does not give the H_1 traces. Their explicit computation and the two permutation-sign twists are additional inputs. After the character is known, rational quotient homology is determined by averaging.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Even without the four-ladder row the sphere is a corollary. The integral character is not a mechanical implication of either antecedent, and the rational subgroup criterion is not treated as an independent originality claim.

The inspected sources do not give the signs of the two graph generators acting on integral homology. The sign-twisted transfer and independent Lefschetz calculation supply that datum. The quotient criterion follows from it by known averaging and is not separately claimed as novel.

value.rationale: On the natural eight-vertex twisted cubic ladder, the homotopy sphere alone cannot diagnose the effect of symmetries on the integral generator. The sign distinguishes the two reflection classes and completely determines which subgroup quotients retain the rational class. That precise graph-action invariant is a useful input to equivariant comparisons of ladder complexes, unlike a recomputation of the known sphere rank.
residual_risks: The value rests on a motivated exact invariant, not a larger ladder classification or a claim about integral or equivariant types of quotients.
